customer_jdoe: Hey team — running into an odd one with streaming responses. Customer reported that the JSON payload from the SSE stream cuts off mid-object when the client reconnects. No `finish_reason` in the final chunk and the client fails to parse. Repro steps + sample: 

customer_jdoe:
> curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" \
>   -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
>   "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=clf-large"
> 
> Received events look like: 
> data: {\"id\":\"resp_abc123\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"{\\\"answer\\\": \"The short...\"\"},\"finish_reason\":null}]}\n> data: {\"id\":\"resp_abc123\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"...continued\\\"}}]}
> <connection drops>
> client reconnects and gets: 
> data: {\"id\":\"resp_abc123\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"\\\"rest\"}}]}
> 
> After concatenation the result is invalid JSON because earlier chunk ended inside a string, e.g. \"The short...continued\\\"rest\". Parser fails and we see no `finish_reason`.

alex (support): Thanks — can you attach the raw tcpdump or a full stream transcript? Also which SDK/client are you using (native EventSource, custom reconnect logic)?

customer_jdoe: Using native EventSource in a React app. We implement naive reconnect on `onerror` and just re-open with same session headers. Raw transcript attached as gist: https://gist.github.com/jdoe/stream-dump-1796 (contains SSE lines). Note: billing for this session shows ~2x expected token count for same prompt (maybe reconnect caused duplication).

maria (eng): I skimmed the gist. Two quick notes: 1) there are partial `data:` frames that end mid-UTF8 string; 2) the reconnect sequence reuses the same `session_id` header but we don't rehydrate server-side streaming state on reconnect — server currently treats the new connection as a fresh stream and sends overlapping continuation fragments. That can produce broken JSON when clients simply concat chunks.

sre-liz: Also seeing spikes in connection reset counts to the region the customer hit (us-west-2) around the same time window. Could be transient network flaps causing the client to reconnect while our runtime was mid-chunk flush.

alex (support): For immediate mitigation, ask the client to: 
1) Buffer `data:` events and only attempt JSON parse when a `\n\n` boundary or an explicit end marker is observed.
2) Add a short jittered backoff before reconnect (e.g., 200-600ms) and pass `X-Resume-From-Offset` header when reopening so we can support resumable streams (we'll add server support).

maria (eng): Internal summary for triage:
- Suspected root cause: non-atomic flush of SSE frames combined with naive client reconnect -> produces overlapping/fragmented JSON objects.
- Repro: use the attached script below to simulate a reconnect while server is sending a large JSON object in pieces.

maria (eng): ```bash
# repro: simulate partial chunk + reconnect
python - <<'PY'
import socket, time
# crude server that emits SSE pieces\s= socket.socket(); s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 18080)); s.listen(1)
conn, _ = s.accept()
conn.recv(1024)
conn.send(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/event-stream\r\
\r\n")
conn.send(b"data: {\"id\":\"r\"")
# drop connection right after partial send to emulate network drop
conn.close()
# client reconnect quickly and reads remaining piece from a new connection (server would issue continuation)
PY
```

maria (eng): Proposed longer-term fixes:
- Server: ensure SSE event atomicity for `data:` events (flush complete JSON records in one framed event). If streaming large payloads, include sequence/offset metadata so clients can resume safely.
- Runtime: add `resume_token` in SSE metadata so reconnects can request resume instead of naive replays.
- Docs: add guidance to SDKs about buffering and resume behavior.

alex (support): For this customer I'm going to create a ticket INC-1796001 and set P1 for public-facing parsing breaks (customer production failure). Also flag billing team to reconcile doubled token counts for session `sess-0492` (might be caused by duplicate replays).

support-bot: Ticket INC-1796001 created and linked to customer_jdoe. SLA window: 24h.

customer_jdoe: Appreciate the quick response. For workaround we'll add a simple delimiter aggregator on the client (wait for `\n\n` or `data: [DONE]`). Can you confirm whether the server ever emits `data: [DONE]` for streaming in this API? We didn't see it in our traces.

maria (eng): Currently our hosted SSE endpoints do not emit an explicit `[DONE]` sentinel in all codepaths — we rely on `finish_reason` inside the JSON. Given fragility here we'll:
- Add explicit `data: [DONE]` on stream completion within 48 hours for hosted API.
- Patch runtime to avoid splitting JSON tokens across SSE event boundaries.

sre-liz: We'll also add a short-term metric to detect fragmented `data:` events (line count per event > 1) and alert on spikes.

alex (support): Action items:
- alex: follow up with customer with a workaround snippet and confirm billing review.
- maria: create PR for atomic `data:` frames + `[DONE]` sentinel.
- sre-liz: add infra alert for fragmented SSE events.
- billing: reconcile `sess-0492` duplication (cc: @billing).

customer_jdoe: thanks — we'll test the client-side aggregator and report back. If you can give an ETA for the server-side patch that'd help our rollout plan.

maria (eng): ETA: 48h for `[DONE]` sentinel; 5 business days for full resume-token feature. Will post PR link here when available.

alex (support): noted — closing this Slack thread for now, will update INC-1796001 and loop in customer once PRs land. :thumbsup:
